description.narrative: The Community Health and Inclusion Association (CHIAs) is a leading Lao non-profit organization with a long-standing commitment to promoting health, well-being, and inclusive development for marginalized communities. Originally founded in 1999 as the LaoYouth AIDS Project (LYAP) and later registered as the Positive Health Association (LaoPHA), CHIA's rebranded in 2020 to reflect its expanded mission—moving beyond HIV/AIDS response to address broader health disparities, social inclusion, and community resilience. Today, CHIAs works with key and vulnerable populations, including LGBTQI+ communities, women and children, migrant workers, people living with diseases, and ethnic minorities, ensuring their access to healthcare, livelihood opportunities, and disaster risk reduction support. CHIAs takes a rights-based, participatory approach, partnering with government agencies, international organizations, and local communities to implement programs in health equity, economic empowerment, and climate resilience. A key focus is Community-Based Disaster Risk Management (CBDRM), where CHIAs builds local capacity to identify risks, develop mitigation strategies, and strengthen preparedness for health and climate-related crises. By integrating gender equality, disability inclusion, and social protection into its initiatives, CHIAs ensures that no one is left behind in development efforts. With over two decades of experience, CHIAs has evolved into a trusted advocate for inclusive development, combining grassroots engagement with policy influence. Its holistic interventions—spanning health education, livelihood training, and disaster resilience—contribute to sustainable wellbeing for Laos’ most at-risk populations. Through collaboration and innovation, CHIAs continues to drive meaningful change, empowering communities to thrive despite systemic challenges.

participating-org.narrative: As of 11 March 2020, our organization has changed our name from Lao Positive Health Association (LaoPHA) to Community Health and Inclusion Association (CHIAs), as approved by the Ministry of Home Affairs, in order to broaden our mandates and more effectively respond to broader needs of our key affected communities. Our organization mandates have been focusing on strengthening community systemto advocate for Community-Led on Health, Nutrition, Rights and Genders for key diversity population, hard to reach groups and People Living with Diseases. The Community Health <(>&<)> Inclusion Association was established under the name ‘Lao Youth AIDS Project: LYAP’ in 1999 and later legally registered under the Association decree 238/PM, 2017.(Reg. No. 94/MOHA) in 2012under the name ‘Lao Positive Health Association: LaoPHA’. In 2020, the organization has rebranded itself to ‘Community Health <(>&<)> Inclusion Association” to reflect our current mandates that have become more diversified, which is to strengthen the communitysystems to advocate for community-led on health, community, rights and genders of vulnerable populations and the inclusion of key populations to take care of their health and social protection effectively by partnering with government agencies and international organizations. The emphasis is on vulnerable populations, including people with sexual diversity, women and children, migrant workers, people living with diseases, ethnic minorities and people inject drugs to be aware of their health, wellbeing and rights protection including being capable of effective response and effective access to relevant government’s services. Our Vision: CHIAs’s vision is to inspire inclusive communities where all key vulnerable populations and diverse groups take leadership to ensure improved health, individual rights and gender equality. Our missions: - Ensure all key vulnerable populations and diverse groups and people living with diseases have effective, affordable and equitable access to healthcare, rights and socialprotection; - Ensure gender equality and sexual rights as well aseradicate violence, human trafficking and all forms of discriminations; - Eradicate hunger and ensure adequate nutrition for all - Strengthen partnership for development
